stem: Under the Articles of Confederation, each state had one vote in Congress. The table shows that this rule meant

options.text: Pennsylvania had the most votes in Congress
options.misconception: Every state had one vote, so no state had the most votes.

options.text: the largest states paid the most taxes to the national government
options.misconception: The table shows population, not taxes. Background: requisitions were set by land value.

options.text: Rhode Island had no vote in Congress
options.misconception: Every state, including Rhode Island, had one vote.

options.text: Virginia and Delaware cast equal votes, though Virginia was far larger

rationales.D: The table gives Virginia 747,610 people and Delaware 59,094, which is more than twelve times as many, yet each state cast one vote in Congress.
rationales.A: Each state had one vote, so Pennsylvania had one vote like every other state.
rationales.B: The table shows population, not taxes. Background: requisitions were set by the value of land.
rationales.C: Rhode Island had one vote in Congress, like every other state.
rationales.general:
1. Read the two numbers. Virginia has 747,610 people; Delaware has 59,094.
2. Divide: 747,610 is more than twelve times 59,094.
3. Background: under the Articles each state cast one vote, whatever its size.
4. The biggest state and the smallest state counted exactly the same in Congress.
Remember: one vote each means the smallest state counted as much as the largest.
